Most of this was already implemented and the bead was stale. ServerName and MailboxName both had into_owned() and to_owned(), and FromStr for the 'static forms — which is the from_owned_dns_name constructor the bead asked for, in idiomatic shape. That covered three of its four caller impacts: storing in a struct, returning from a function that took owned input, and satisfying 'static bounds.

The fourth was genuinely unmet and was the point: 'caches need 'static keys'. Neither type derived Hash or Ord, so reaching 'static bought nothing — HashMap<ServerName<'static>, _> did not compile either way. Both derives are now in. Both were needed, not just Hash: HashMap is std-only and pkix-identity is in the workspace's no-std set, so a bare-metal consumer keys a BTreeMap and needs Ord.

The derives agree with Eq, which is what makes them useful: Cow compares and hashes its contents, so a borrowed name and an owned name for one host are a single key and a borrowed lookup finds an owned entry. Covered by an_owned_server_name_keys_both_kinds_of_map and an_owned_mailbox_name_keys_both_kinds_of_map, the latter also pinning that the domain is case-folded before the key forms while the local-part stays case-sensitive per RFC 5321 §2.4. Mutation-verified: dropping the derives fails compilation with 7 trait-bound errors.

Decision on the bead's three options, which it said had to be made before 1.0: option (b). Keep the 'a parameter, keep the escape hatch. Option (a) — drop 'a to match rustls-pki-types — would break every dependent for no capability we now lack, and would cost the zero-allocation borrowed path that the no-std consumers are the reason for. Pre-1.0 plus #[non_exhaustive] leaves (a) open if that trade is ever worth revisiting.

Shipped in pkix-identity 0.3.1 (unpublished). CI green on 97dc9036.
